targets.title: Frame-header decode, canonical 7/16/64-bit payload lengths, masking
targets.statement: The shipped frame-header decoder and mask function: translateSingleFrame / translateSingleFramePayloadLength decode the 7-bit inline, 126->16-bit, and 127->64-bit big-endian payload-length forms via sign-carrying BigInteger parse, with the parsed length range-checked in translateSingleFrameCheckLengthLimit (648-661:>Integer.MAX_VALUE / >maxFrameSize / <0 rejection), and the XOR mask loop is applied on encode for the client role and removed on decode. The shipped packet-size accounting is NOT checked arithmetic: realpacketsize is a plain int accumulator (534) advanced by unchecked additions (+2/+8 length-escape bytes at 622/629, +4 mask at 553, += payloadlength at 554) that can overflow to a negative value BEFORE translateSingleFrameCheckPacketSize compares it (555, 670-676); with maxFrameSize at its Integer.MAX_VALUE default (210), a payloadlength near Integer.MAX_VALUE wraps the accumulator and defeats the completeness comparison — overflow-before-check is representable in the shipped code. Proof obligations bind to these shipped behaviors only.

java_authority.behavior: translateSingleFrame: FIN/RSV/opcode/mask-bit header decode; realpacketsize is a plain int accumulator (534) advanced by unchecked additions (+4 mask at 553, += payloadlength at 554) and only afterwards compared by translateSingleFrameCheckPacketSize (555) — int overflow before the comparison is representable; decode-side unmask XOR loop over the 4-byte key (558-563); checkAlloc-guarded payload allocation (557).

translateSingleFramePayloadLength: 7-bit inline lengths; 126 -> 16-bit and 127 -> 64-bit big-endian decode via sign-carrying BigInteger; control frames with >125 octets rejected at the escape (617-620); the shipped decoder does NOT reject non-minimal 16/64-bit encodings.

translateSingleFrameCheckLengthLimit: length > Integer.MAX_VALUE, length > maxFrameSize, and length < 0 all throw LimitExceededException — explicit range checks on the already-parsed long payload length, NOT overflow-checked arithmetic on the packet-size accumulator (see 553-555).
createByteBufferFromFramedata: role masking (mask = role == Role.CLIENT at 480); 4-byte random mask key emission and XOR loop (511-517); 126/127 marker bytes and length-byte emission (497-510).
getSizeBytes: encode-side size-class selection (<=125 -> 1, <=65535 -> 2, else 8).
toByteArray: big-endian emission of the encoded payload length.

targets.title: Allocation caps on the frame decode path
targets.statement: Frame-decode-path allocations are guarded site-by-site by the shipped code: the three translate-path ByteBuffer.allocate sites are wrapped in Draft.checkAlloc (negative byte counts throw InvalidDataException(PROTOCOL_ERROR)) — payload (Draft_6455.java:557), incomplete-frame extension (749), and incomplete-frame stash (768) — with the payload size bounded by maxFrameSize via translateSingleFrameCheckLengthLimit. The fragmented-message reassembly allocation (getPayloadFromByteBufferList, 1171) is NOT checkAlloc-wrapped; it is bounded by checkBufferLimit (at most maxFrameSize, invoked at 1170). Encode-path allocations (482, 512) carry no checkAlloc guard and are outside this claim. Proof obligations for allocation caps bind to these shipped guards exactly as sited.

java_authority.behavior: Draft.checkAlloc: bytecount < 0 throws InvalidDataException(CloseFrame.PROTOCOL_ERROR); wrapped around the translate-path ByteBuffer.allocate sites (Draft_6455.java:557, 749, 768) — NOT around the reassembly allocation (1171), which checkBufferLimit bounds instead.
translateSingleFrame: checkAlloc-guarded payload allocation (557) after packet-size revalidation (555).
translateFrame incomplete-frame path: checkAlloc-guarded buffer growth for extendedframe (749) and incompleteframe (768).

getPayloadFromByteBufferList: the reassembly ByteBuffer.allocate((int) totalSize) at 1171 is guarded by checkBufferLimit (1170) rather than Draft.checkAlloc; totalSize is at most maxFrameSize when the allocation runs.

targets.title: Control-frame constraints (<=125 octets, opcode discrimination, dispatch)
targets.statement: Control frames (CLOSING/PING/PONG) with payload length above 125 octets are rejected at the 16/64-bit length escape; opcodes are discriminated by fromOpcode/toOpcode with unknown opcodes rejected; processFrame dispatches close/ping/pong in the shipped order. Proof obligations bind to these shipped constraints.

java_authority.behavior: translateSingleFramePayloadLength: PING/PONG/CLOSING reaching the >125 escape throw InvalidFrameException("more than 125 octets").
processFrame: CLOSING -> processFrameClosing, PING -> onWebsocketPing, PONG -> updateLastPong + onWebsocketPong, data frames -> continuation/fin handling.
fromOpcode/toOpcode: opcode discrimination; unknown opcode bytes throw InvalidFrameException.

targets.title: Server handshake accept predicate and Sec-WebSocket-Accept derivation
targets.statement: The SHIPPED server accept predicate is permissive: acceptHandshakeAsServer gates only readVersion(handshake) == 13 (any Integer.parseInt spelling after trim), and postProcessHandshakeResponseAsServer rejects only a null/empty Sec-WebSocket-Key before deriving Sec-WebSocket-Accept via the RFC 6455 SHA-1 derivation over the trimmed key. Draft.basicAccept's Upgrade/Connection validation runs only on the client path. Proof obligations for accept-derivation encode this shipped predicate; RFC-stricter reject language is valid only as a ledgered behavior delta.

java_authority.behavior: acceptHandshakeAsServer: NOT_MATCHED only when readVersion != 13; extension/protocol matching accepts with the shipped defaults (DefaultExtension and Protocol("")).
readVersion: Integer.parseInt after trim — '+13', '0013', ' 13 ' all read as 13; unparseable values read as -1.
postProcessHandshakeResponseAsServer: throws InvalidHandshakeException only for a missing/empty Sec-WebSocket-Key; sets Sec-WebSocket-Accept from generateFinalKey.
generateFinalKey: SHA-1 over trimmed key + RFC 6455 GUID, Base64-encoded — the accept derivation equals the RFC value.

targets.title: Terminal close is absorbing; terminal delivery is at-least-once (reentrant duplicate representable)
targets.statement: closeConnection is the only shipped terminal transition: readyState = CLOSED is assigned solely at WebSocketImpl.java:566, the method is monitor-guarded (synchronized, 530), and re-entry AFTER the terminal transition returns immediately (readyState == CLOSED guard, 531-533). The shipped ordering delivers the terminal onWebsocketClose callback (556-561) BEFORE setting readyState = CLOSED (566), and Java monitors are reentrant, so a listener that re-enters closeConnection from inside onWebsocketClose (any overload, 569-582) passes the 531-533 guard while readyState is still not CLOSED and receives a second terminal callback: the shipped observable semantics are at-least-once terminal delivery — exactly-once holds across threads (monitor plus guard) and for listeners that do not re-enter the close path, but reentrant duplicate delivery is representable in the shipped code. After the callback the draft is reset (562-564) and CLOSED is set (566). flushAndClose's flushandclosestate latch is set (592) BEFORE its onWebsocketClosing callback (597), so close initiation is idempotent even under callback re-entry, and it records the close code/message/remote triple (588-590) that the latched terminal path delivers verbatim. Proof obligations bind to these shipped semantics.

java_authority.behavior: closeConnection: immediate return only once readyState is already CLOSED (531-533); terminal onWebsocketClose delivered (556-561) BEFORE readyState = CLOSED is set (566); the synchronized monitor (530) is reentrant, so same-thread re-entry from inside the callback passes the 531-533 guard and duplicates the terminal callback — at-least-once delivery, not exactly-once; draft reset (562-564); readyState = CLOSED (566).

flushAndClose: flushandclosestate latch set (592) BEFORE the onWebsocketClosing callback (597), so initiation is idempotent including under callback re-entry; records closecode/closemessage/closedremotely (588-590); onWebsocketClosing delivered once.

targets.title: Connection state machine: no transition escapes CLOSED
targets.statement: The four shipped states NOT_YET_CONNECTED/OPEN/CLOSING/CLOSED transition only forward: open() sets OPEN from the handshake-complete path, close() initiates CLOSING under the monitor, eot() funnels every EOF into closeConnection, and no shipped path leaves CLOSED. The decode gate processes frames only in OPEN. Proof obligations bind to these shipped transitions.

java_authority.behavior: ReadyState: the closed four-state vocabulary NOT_YET_CONNECTED, OPEN, CLOSING, CLOSED.
close(int,String,boolean): monitor-guarded CLOSING transition with single close-frame send; no-ops once CLOSING/CLOSED.

open: readyState = OPEN set (759) BEFORE onWebsocketOpen is delivered (761-765), and decode reaches the completed-handshake path only from NOT_YET_CONNECTED, so the OPEN transition fires exactly once on the serialized decode path (unlike closeConnection, the state is set before the callback, so callback re-entry cannot duplicate it); onWebsocketOpen delivered.
eot: every EOF dispatch funnels into closeConnection (NEVER_CONNECTED / latched code / NORMAL / ABNORMAL_CLOSE); no path resurrects a closed connection.
decode: frames are decoded only in OPEN; NOT_YET_CONNECTED bytes go to decodeHandshake; no state regression from the decode path.

targets.title: Total UTF-8 validation of text payloads
targets.statement: Text payloads are validated by the shipped CharsetDecoder configured with CodingErrorAction.REPORT: every complete text payload delivered to onWebsocketMessage passes stringUtf8 (unfragmented at Draft_6455.java:986, reassembled at 1013), and every malformed or unmappable sequence throws InvalidDataException(NO_UTF8). The shipped isValidUTF8 screen applies ONLY to the initial TEXT-opcode fragment of a fragmented sequence (940-943); intermediate CONTINUOUS fragments are not incrementally validated, so invalid UTF-8 arriving in them is detected only at the fin-frame stringUtf8 pass. The Rust port must reject the identical sequence set at the same shipped observation points. Proof obligations bind to these shipped validators.

java_authority.behavior: stringUtf8: CharsetDecoder with CodingErrorAction.REPORT (44); CharacterCodingException maps to InvalidDataException(CloseFrame.NO_UTF8).

isValidUTF8: incremental DFA validity check; the shipped decode path invokes it only for the initial TEXT-opcode fragment of a fragmented sequence (Draft_6455.java:940-943), never for CONTINUOUS continuation fragments.
processFrameText: every complete text payload passes Charsetfunctions.stringUtf8 before onWebsocketMessage.

targets.title: Bounded fragmentation reassembly
targets.statement: Continuation reassembly enforces its size bound at two shipped checkpoints, not per-append: the sequence-start fragment appends then checks (processFrameIsNotFin, Draft_6455.java:1044-1045) and the fin frame appends then checks before delivery (processFrameIsFin, 1006-1007); when the reassembled total exceeds maxFrameSize, checkBufferLimit clears the buffer list and throws LimitExceededException (1101-1109, clear at 1104). Intermediate CONTINUOUS non-fin fragments are appended WITHOUT a checkBufferLimit call (processFrameContinuousAndNonFin, append at 946), so the shipped buffer list can exceed maxFrameSize and keep growing while non-fin continuations keep arriving — unbounded intermediate growth is representable in the shipped code until the fin checkpoint re-imposes the bound (or getPayloadFromByteBufferList re-checks at 1170). Sequencing violations (unstarted or uncompleted sequences) are protocol errors (905-908, 934-938, 1001-1005, 1038-1042). Proof obligations bind to these shipped checkpoint semantics only.

java_authority.behavior: checkBufferLimit: reassembly total > maxFrameSize clears the buffer list (1104) and throws LimitExceededException(maxFrameSize); invoked at sequence start (1045), at fin (1007), and inside getPayloadFromByteBufferList (1170) — NOT for intermediate CONTINUOUS non-fin appends (946).

processFrameContinuousAndNonFin: continuation sequencing; unstarted continuation is a PROTOCOL_ERROR (934-938); the isValidUTF8 screen runs only when the frame opcode is TEXT — the initial fragment (940-943) — never for CONTINUOUS fragments; intermediate CONTINUOUS non-fin payloads are appended (946) without a checkBufferLimit call.
processFrameIsFin: append + checkBufferLimit before reassembled delivery; buffer list cleared after delivery.
processFrameIsNotFin: sequence start; append under the cap; uncompleted-previous-sequence is a PROTOCOL_ERROR.

targets.title: Adapters carry no protocol logic
targets.statement: WebSocketImpl.decode is the single protocol ingress: the shipped I/O helpers move bytes verbatim between sockets and the engine and never interpret WebSocket framing or handshakes. The Rust adapters (US-018) must preserve this byte-stream transparency; the proof target prohibits protocol logic outside ws_core. Proof obligations bind to this shipped separation.

java_authority.behavior: decode(ByteBuffer): the single protocol ingress the adapters feed; adapters never interpret WebSocket bytes.
SocketChannelIOHelper.read/readMore: pure byte transport from the channel into the engine buffer; no protocol interpretation.
SocketChannelIOHelper.batch: drains engine-produced buffers to the socket verbatim; the only protocol-adjacent effect (server-role close-on-drain) is delegated back to the engine via closeConnection.

targets.title: Single-owner serialization replaces the shared-mutable connection state
targets.statement: Java's connection state is shared-mutable — unbounded outQueue/inQueue, one volatile readyState read cross-thread without the monitor, the synchronizeWriteObject write lock, and the instance monitor across close/closeConnection/flushAndClose. The port's single-owner design serializes commands and inbound actions through one owner per connection; race-visible Java interleavings are not corpus-encodable and Java fidelity is defined over serialized observable event sequences. Proof obligations bind to the owner-serialization design, never to racy Java interleavings.

java_authority.behavior: The shared mutable state the port serializes: unbounded outQueue/inQueue (96-102) and the volatile readyState (127) read cross-thread without the monitor.
write(List) under synchronizeWriteObject: multi-frame enqueue of one message is atomic against other senders — wire order within a message is observable.

The instance monitor across close/closeConnection/flushAndClose is the de-facto connection lock: it yields exactly-once close initiation (flushandclosestate latch set at 592 before the onWebsocketClosing callback at 597) and cross-thread mutual exclusion for terminal delivery, but the monitor is reentrant and closeConnection fires onWebsocketClose (557) before setting CLOSED (566), so same-thread callback re-entry can duplicate the terminal callback — see target.formal.close.terminal-absorbing.

java_authority_members: org.java_websocket.WebSocketImpl (shared-mutable state consolidated into the single owner)
